newsitem.title: UK: British consumers flock to themed restaurants.
newsitem.headline: British consumers flock to themed restaurants.

text.p: British consumers are flocking to eat at themed restaurants, where the food often plays second fiddle to the atmosphere and T-shirt sales contribute as much to profits as the menu, market research company Mintel said on Wednesday.

Sport, fashion and film themed restaurants are already established in London and will be joined soon by a Rainforest Cafe -- complete with parrots and a waterfall -- and by a Jekyll and Hyde Horror Club.
Mintel estimates that by the year 2001 British consumers will spend 250 million pounds ($407.8 million) on what it calls the leisure experience.
"The atmosphere and experience offered at the theme restaurant is certainly as important as the food for the majority of diners," said Mintel's Leisure Intelligence report.
Themed restaurants offer diners film clips of sporting events, movies or fashion shows and the walls are usually decked with appropriate memorabilia.
Themed restaurants are particularly popular with the young. Over two thirds of adults under age 25 have visited a theme restaurant, Mintel said.
Fans frequently visit concept restaurants such as the Hard Rock Cafe or the Fashion Cafe expecting to bump into the restaurants' highly publicised celebrity partners.

The Planet Hollywood International Inc chain is backed by film stars Arnold Schwarzenegger, Sylvester Stallone, Bruce Willis and Demi Moore. London's Fashion Cafe is endorsed by supermodels Claudia Schiffer, Naomi Campbell and Elle Macpherson.
"In practice, however, the involvement of mega stars is limited," said the Mintel report.
Having eaten a burger at the Hard Rock Cafe or a low-calorie salad at the Fashion Cafe, many diners then buy a T-shirt as a souvenir of their visit.

"Merchandising plays a major role in the themed restaurant turnover, accounting for 50 percent of Hard Rock's total and between 20 percent and 40 percent at other outlets. Critics suggest that merchandising is of more importance to themed restaurant operators than the food," Mintel said.

The report said conditions exist for a steady rise in themed restaurants, but as consumers become increasingly sophisticated outlets will have to offer more in the way of value for money, service and atmosphere.
It added that their success will not be dictated by the theme chosen but by the quality of the execution.
